summary: Legal review of pricing guidance language (usage definitions, disputes, credits) for Sales Enablement + Confluence
description:
Request Legal review/approval of updated internal pricing guidance language before Sales Enablement rollout and before we reuse wording in MSAs/order forms.

Background
Finance + Product + Eng are hardening billing meters (tokens/requests, cache-hit attribution, retries/idempotency behavior) and updating internal pricing/packaging guidance. We need Legal to confirm that internal/customer-facing language is accurate, consistent with our current contract positions, and does not create implied guarantees that we can’t operationalize.

Scope of Legal review
1) Usage definitions (Hosted API)
- Define “token” for billing purposes (prompt vs completion; billed_tokens vs raw tokens) and clarify that models/tokenizers vary.
- Clarify treatment of streaming responses (partial chunks, client disconnects) and what is billable when output was generated server-side.
- Clarify tool/function calling and structured output token attribution.
- Clarify retries/fallback behavior (server-side retries, fallback routing, idempotency) and how we prevent double-counting.
- Clarify caching behavior and cache-hit attribution (when cache reduces billed tokens and how it appears in usage exports).

2) Disputes, credits, and invoice adjustments
- Dispute window language (timeline; evidence required; how we handle late-arriving telemetry/backfills).
- Credits/refunds guardrails: when credits may be issued, approval path, and how credits apply to usage meters.
- Avoid committing to retroactive changes without Finance/Legal sign-off; ensure language preserves forward-fix preference.

3) Consistency checks
- Ensure wording is consistent across: Sales FAQ, Product pricing pages (internal), RevRec procedures, and clause library.
- Confirm any “audit log / usage export” promises align with the metering data retention & access controls policy.

Artifacts for review (links)
- Sales Enablement draft FAQ (Hosted API): sources/confluence/sales-enablement/pricing-guidance/hosted-api-pricing-faq-and-objection-handling.json
- Usage-based pricing legal terms playbook + clause library: sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/contracts-and-legal-process/usage-based-pricing-legal-terms-playbook.json
- Free tier + overage policy language (internal): sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/hosted-api-packages-free-tier-and-overage-policy.json
- Discounts & credits policy (internal): sources/confluence/product-docs/pricing-and-packaging/discounting-and-credits-policy-for-usage-based-products.json
- Hosted API meter spec (reference for definitions): sources/confluence/finance-and-legal/revrec-and-billing/billing-meter-spec-hosted-api-tokens-and-requests.json
- Metering data retention & access controls (reference): sources/confluence/policies-and-process/data-management/metering-data-retention-and-access-controls.json

What we need from Legal (acceptance criteria)
- Approval (or redlines) on the exact recommended customer-facing phrasing for:
  a) “billed tokens vs raw tokens” explanation
  b) retries/fallback + idempotency wording (avoid implying we never retry)
  c) caching / cache-hit attribution wording
  d) dispute window + credit issuance language
- Confirm whether any phrases should be marked “internal only” vs acceptable for customer-facing collateral.
- Identify any changes required to the clause library or contracting playbook to align with new guidance.

Timeline / urgency
Target to finalize language by 2026-02-26 to support end-of-month enablement and to avoid conflicting messaging during ongoing pricing experiments.

Notes / constraints
- Meter semantics are evolving under shadow-billing compare mode; avoid language that implies absolute immutability of meter internals. We can commit to stable definitions and transparent usage exports, but need to preserve ability to fix bugs.
- This ticket is for review/approval and wording guidance only; meter implementation work is tracked separately in Eng/Product systems.

Owner coordination
Primary contacts: Elliot Price (docs), Nikhil Sharma (Product), Emily Stone (RevRec), Sofia Mendes (Commercial Counsel), Michael Grant (GC, usage terms).
comments: 2026-02-13 10:18 PT — Elliot Price (Reporter): Opening for Legal review. The Sales FAQ draft is ready for redlines; key contentious areas are (1) streaming disconnect billing explanation and (2) retries/fallback wording. Tagging Sofia + Michael. Target approval by 2/26.

2026-02-14 09:42 PT — Sofia Mendes (Assignee): Acknowledged. Please paste the exact candidate paragraphs you want approved (not just links) so we can track deltas. Also confirm intended audience: customer-facing email + Sales deck vs internal Confluence only.

2026-02-14 11:05 PT — Elliot Price: Added candidate paragraphs to the FAQ page under section “Billed vs raw tokens / caching / retries”. Intended to be customer-facing for AEs/SEs (email copy OK). Not intended as binding contractual language, but likely to be quoted in procurement threads.

2026-02-17 16:30 PT — Michael Grant: Initial pass: avoid “we only bill for tokens you receive” — streaming/server-side generation can be billable even if client disconnects. Recommend: “we bill for tokens generated by the service for your request, subject to documented meter rules; usage exports show billed tokens.” Also add a sentence that tokenization varies by model and we publish billed_tokens as the source of truth for billing.

2026-02-18 13:12 PT — Emily Stone: +1 to clarifying “billed_tokens is source of truth.” Also please avoid implying we’ll do retroactive invoice changes automatically; we need Finance approval and audit trail. Suggest: disputes within X days; adjustments via credit memo when approved.

2026-02-20 10:06 PT — Sofia Mendes: Proposed dispute/credit language: 30-day dispute window from invoice date; customer must provide request IDs/time range and usage export evidence. Redwood will investigate and may issue credits in its discretion where metering error is confirmed. No retroactive rate changes; meter bug fixes apply prospectively unless otherwise agreed in writing.

2026-02-21 15:27 PT — Nikhil Sharma: Confirmed 30 days works for self-serve and sales-led. For enterprise, we sometimes see 45 days requested—can we keep internal guidance at 30 and allow exceptions via contracting playbook?

2026-02-22 09:18 PT — Sofia Mendes: Yes—internal guidance can say “standard 30 days; enterprise exceptions require Legal approval.” Please add that to the Sales FAQ as an internal note, not customer-facing.

2026-02-24 17:40 PT — Elliot Price: Updated FAQ draft with Legal’s wording: removed “only bill for tokens you receive,” added streaming caveat, clarified retries/fallback and idempotency as “deduped by request id/idempotency key,” and added dispute/credit section with 30-day standard + exception path. Requesting final approval so we can close this ticket and proceed with enablement.
